Name: canonicalization_convergence
Title: Mental Paraphrase: Do LLMs Normalize a Problem Toward a Canonical Form Before Reasoning, and Do Failures Come From Not Getting There?
Short Hypothesis: Before reasoning, an LLM internally normalizes a problem's varied surface phrasings toward a shared canonical representation ('mental paraphrase'); reasoning errors on awkward or unfamiliar surface forms are caused by incomplete convergence to that canonical form rather than by the reasoning steps themselves, and the degree of convergence is a readable, causal signal that predicts correctness and can be causally restored by injecting the canonical representation. Primary novelty separator: convergence is measured at the PRE-reasoning problem representation (before any reasoning token), distinguishing a canonicalization bottleneck from convergence that only appears during answer production; the canonical form is defined by multiple operationalizations (centroid, medoid, consensus latent, pairwise convergence) rather than by frequent/terse phrasing alone.
Related Work: Prior work documents that LLMs are brittle to surface form: subtle rephrasings change math solve rates (Paraphrase and Solve / SCoP, 2024), reasoning traces are robust to some CoT interventions but not style-invariant and paraphrasing shortens traces and harms accuracy (Are Reasoning LLMs Robust to Interventions on Their CoT?, 2026), and CoT is often unfaithful (Measuring Faithfulness in CoT, 2023). Representation studies show reasoning representations converge across languages when reasoning succeeds (Under the Shadow of Babel, 2025), that NMT paraphrase-invariance is largely shallow (Neurons Invariant to Sentence Structural Changes, 2022), and that abstract concept vectors exist but are not always output-invariant (Concept Vectors, 2025; Abstract Activation Spaces, 2026). Content-effect work steers a 'validity vs plausibility' direction to debias reasoning (How LMs Conflate Validity with Plausibility, 2025; K-CAST, 2025). ALL of these are either (a) behavioral surface-form robustness studies with no internal mechanism, or (b) steering of a content/validity concept. NONE propose that the model performs an internal canonicalization step that maps diverse phrasings toward a shared normal form before reasoning, that reasoning failure is caused by INCOMPLETE convergence to that canonical form, that per-item convergence is a diagnostic signal of correctness, or that injecting the canonical representation causally rescues hard-phrasing errors. My prior proposals covered word-order, morphology, tokenization granularity, lexical gaps, and grammatical-mood effects, but none address surface-form-invariant canonicalization as a locatable, causal computation. We uniquely reframe paraphrase brittleness from a behavioral quirk into a mechanistic canonicalization-convergence account with a Location + Causal Intervention strategy and a high-stakes clinical instance. Delta and alternative mechanisms: prior representation-convergence work (Under the Shadow of Babel 2025) observes convergence during SUCCESSFUL reasoning, whereas we test whether INCOMPLETE pre-reasoning convergence CAUSES failure. We explicitly pre-register and discriminate competing explanations for the convergence-accuracy link -- confidence, pretraining familiarity, shallow lexical normalization, and retrieval-to-nearest-pretraining-neighbor -- rather than assuming a canonicalization mechanism, and 'canonical form' is defined rigorously (multiple operationalizations, held-out layer selection) so it does not collapse into an embedding-centroid or terse-style artifact.
Abstract: Large language models solve the same problem at different rates depending only on how it is worded, yet why remains unclear. We propose a mechanistic account: before reasoning, the model performs a 'mental paraphrase', normalizing a problem's diverse surface forms toward a shared canonical representation, and reasoning failures on awkward or unfamiliar phrasings arise because the model never fully reaches that canonical form. We make three claims. First, canonicalization is real and graded: across paraphrase clusters (many wordings of one problem), the internal representations converge toward a common form in intermediate layers, and convergence is stronger for the phrasings the model solves correctly. Second, convergence is diagnostic: per-item distance from the paraphrase cluster's canonical representation predicts whether that phrasing will be solved, beyond confidence and entropy, and pinpoints which surface forms are 'lost in translation' before any reasoning error appears. Third, convergence is causal, not incidental: patching the canonical representation (derived from easy, frequent phrasings) into the model's processing of a hard phrasing rescues correctness, and steering along a located 'canonicalization' direction moves reasoning accuracy up or down. We test these on math, logic, and multi-hop QA with controlled paraphrase clusters spanning register, syntax, and verbosity across several open-weight models, plus a high-stakes clinical instance where a benign rephrasing of a case description silently degrades diagnostic accuracy through failed canonicalization. Our work reframes paraphrase brittleness as incomplete internal normalization and offers an interpretable pre-reasoning failure signal and a training-free rescue. Deployment implications if confirmed: new robustness metrics (pre-reasoning convergence as a wording-fragility score), targeted data augmentation toward hard phrasings, and inference-time repair by canonical-representation patching; the communities most likely to reuse the artifacts are mechanistic interpretability, robustness/evaluation, safety, and medical NLP. Either outcome is useful -- a positive result gives intervention targets, a null rules out a prominent mechanism and redirects robustness research toward reasoning-stage sensitivity. We temper the clinical claim from 'misdiagnosis' to model error under a defined error taxonomy (colloquial-vs-formal phrasing of identical findings), framed as user-facing reliability for multilingual, colloquial, and accessibility-sensitive interfaces.
Experiments:
Shared setup (applies to every experiment below): all runs use five frozen open-weight models -- Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Gemma-2-9B -- with no weight updates; the only trainable parameters anywhere are linear-probe weights on frozen hidden states. Decoding is greedy for primary conditions and temperature 0.7 for sampled conditions, each sampled run over seeds 0, 1, 2. Effect sizes carry 95% bootstrap CIs over 1000 item-level resamples; behavioral tests use mixed-effects regression with crossed random intercepts. "Canonicalization convergence" means the degree to which the internal representations of many wordings of one problem approach a shared form before reasoning; the "Convergence Score" is negative distance from a phrasing's pre-reasoning representation to its cluster's canonical (frequent/terse-formal) centroid at the layer of maximal within-cluster convergence.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Canonicalization is real, graded, and stronger for correctly solved phrasings): Tests within-cluster convergence and its link to correctness. Data: for each base problem we build a cluster of 8-12 meaning-preserving paraphrases spanning controlled axes (register formal/colloquial, syntax simple/embedded, verbosity terse/padded, voice active/passive), over 200 base problems from the GSM8K test split (1,319 available), 200 from the MATH test split (5,000 available), 150 synthetic deductive-logic chains (depth 2-6, auto-checkable), and 150 from the 2WikiMultiHopQA dev set (12,576 available), 700 clusters / roughly 5,600-8,400 phrasings; paraphrases are generated by templated transforms plus an LLM paraphraser and meaning-preservation is verified by back-translation and human spot-check on a 10% sample. 700 clusters gives enough within-cluster behavioral variance for stable convergence estimates within budget. We extract pre-reasoning hidden states at the end-of-problem position per phrasing per layer, compute within-cluster dispersion by layer and each phrasing's distance to the canonical centroid, controlling for length and word-overlap by regression. Decisive metric first: within-cluster representational dispersion as a function of layer (does it fall to a minimum in intermediate layers?) and the Convergence Score difference between correctly and incorrectly solved phrasings; secondary: the layer of maximal convergence per model. Convincing result: dispersion shows a clear intermediate-layer minimum and correctly solved phrasings have reliably higher Convergence Score than incorrect ones (CI excludes 0) after controlling for length/word-overlap. Indecision band: a correct-minus-incorrect Convergence difference whose CI lies within +/-0.05 standardized units means convergence is not graded by correctness. Negative result: flat dispersion across layers or no correctness link means there is no canonicalization computation, refuting H1.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- Convergence is diagnostic of solve probability before reasoning): Tests pre-reasoning error prediction. Data: the same clusters, split 70/30 by cluster. Decisive metric first: from mixed-effects logistic regression correct ~ Convergence + length + word_overlap + (1|cluster)+(1|model), the Convergence coefficient's significance beyond shallow features; secondary: held-out AUROC of a probe on Convergence features for predicting correctness versus verbalized confidence, token entropy, and per-token surprisal baselines. Convincing result: Convergence retains a reliable positive coefficient beyond length/word-overlap (CI excludes 0) and its AUROC exceeds the best baseline by >= 0.05, measured before any reasoning tokens. Indecision band: a Convergence coefficient CI overlapping 0, or delta-AUROC within +/-0.03, means convergence carries no diagnostic value beyond shallow similarity. Negative result: no predictive power refutes H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- Patching the canonical representation causally rescues hard-phrasing errors): Tests the causal rescue. Data: hard phrasings the model fails, paired with an easy/canonical phrasing of the SAME problem. We cache the pre-reasoning representation from the canonical phrasing and patch it into the hard-phrasing forward pass at the convergence layer. Controls: patch from a DIFFERENT problem's canonical representation (specificity), patch a random-matched representation, and no-patch baseline; we verify no answer tokens are present in the patched pre-reasoning representation (rules out answer-leakage). Decisive metric first: accuracy recovery on failed hard phrasings under same-problem canonical patching versus no-patch; secondary: same-problem versus cross-problem/random patching. Convincing result: same-problem canonical patching recovers accuracy by >= 8 points (CI excludes 0) while cross-problem and random patching do not (within 2 points of no-patch). Indecision band: a same-problem recovery within +/-3 points, or a same-versus-cross gap within +/-3 points, means patching does not selectively restore canonicalization. Negative result: no selective recovery, or equal recovery from cross-problem patches, refutes the causal canonicalization-bottleneck claim (and would indicate answer-leakage if cross-problem also rescues).

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Steering a canonicalization direction moves accuracy): Tests the mechanism's generality. Data: matched converged-minus-non-converged phrasing contrasts (content matched) yield a difference-in-means "canonicalization" direction at the convergence layer. Systems: plus-direction steering on hard phrasings, minus-direction on easy phrasings, random-direction of matched norm, no-steer. Decisive metric first: accuracy gain from plus-direction steering on hard phrasings versus random-direction; secondary: minus-direction induced failure on easy phrasings, dose-response, whether per-item convergence increase from patching/steering predicts per-item accuracy gain (Spearman), and specificity (easy-item accuracy within 1 point, fluency preserved). Convincing result: plus-direction steering raises hard-phrasing accuracy by >= 3 points over random-direction (CI excludes 0) with monotonic dose-response and preserved easy-item accuracy, minus-direction lowers easy-phrasing accuracy, and convergence change mediates the gain. Indecision band: steering effects within +/-2 points of random-direction leave the direction unproven; the patching result (Experiment 3) then stands alone. Negative result: no steerable effect means the canonicalization direction is not causal.

Experiment 5 (H1/H3 -- High-stakes clinical instance): Tests whether colloquial phrasing degrades diagnosis through failed canonicalization and patching rescues it. Data: 300 clinical case clusters adapted from MedQA (USMLE, 12,723 questions), each pairing colloquial patient-reported phrasing with formal chart phrasing of identical findings for a differential-diagnosis task; 300 supports paired contrasts under expert spot-checking. Decisive metric first: confident-misdiagnosis rate on colloquial versus formal phrasings, and its relation to a lower Convergence Score on colloquial phrasings; secondary: misdiagnosis reduction under canonical-representation patching on fine-distinction cases. Convincing result: colloquial phrasings show lower convergence and higher confident misdiagnosis, and canonical patching reduces misdiagnosis by >= 5 points (CIs exclude 0). Indecision band: a colloquial-versus-formal gap or patching effect within +/-2 points is inconclusive for high-stakes transfer. Negative result: no phrasing effect on diagnosis, or no patching rescue, bounds the claim to benign benchmarks.

Experiment 6 (Rigorous operationalization, shallow-similarity controls, and competing-hypothesis discrimination): The convergence layer is selected on held-out clusters (nested evaluation) to avoid post-hoc picking. We report robustness across multiple canonicalization operationalizations (centroid, medoid phrasing, consensus latent, pairwise convergence, and a latent-factor model). Against shallow similarity we add matched lexical-overlap subsets, adversarial paraphrases with matched length and word-overlap, and analyses on representations residualized against lexical features. Causal patching (Experiment 3) is validated with timing sweeps, token-position sweeps, and partial-patch ablations, and we verify rescue is not generic confidence inflation and is answer-identity specific -- same-item canonical patching rescues the correct answer but does NOT transfer to semantically related distractor items. We add discriminating tests for the competing mechanisms (pretraining familiarity, retrieval-to-neighbor, parser load, difficulty/confidence) and report expected detectable effect sizes/power for the rescue and steering thresholds across 7B-14B models. Paraphrase quality assurance is strengthened with expert review and explicit exclusion criteria for MedQA and math clusters.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) Convergence may be a shallow artifact of lexical/length similarity rather than genuine semantic canonicalization; mitigated by controlling for length/word-overlap in all analyses, by the NMT-paraphrase-style confound checks, and by the causal patching test (which holds content fixed and manipulates only the representation). (2) Paraphrases may not be perfectly meaning-preserving, confounding 'hard phrasing' with subtle meaning shifts; mitigated by back-translation and human verification and by using controlled templated transforms. (3) Instruction-tuned models may be robustly paraphrase-invariant, flattening convergence differences (ceiling); we include harder/awkward phrasings, multiple models, and base variants, and focus on clusters with genuine behavioral variance. (4) The convergence layer may vary across models/tasks; we scan all layers and report the layer of maximal within-cluster convergence per model. (5) Same-problem patching could rescue accuracy simply by leaking the answer rather than restoring canonicalization; we patch only the PRE-reasoning problem representation (before any solution content), verify no answer tokens are present, and use cross-problem/random patching specificity controls. (6) The canonicalization direction may entangle with generic difficulty/confidence; addressed by matched converged/non-converged contrasts, random-direction steering, and easy-item specificity checks. (7) Effects may be small or model-specific; we test multiple models and report effect sizes with CIs. (8) A null result (convergence does not predict or cause correctness) is itself informative: it would indicate paraphrase brittleness is not driven by a canonicalization bottleneck but by reasoning-stage sensitivity, distinguishing surface-form failures from representation-normalization failures. (9) The 'mental paraphrase' framing is operationalized representationally and causally, not as a claim of human-like paraphrasing. (10) We report the clinical outcome as model error under a defined error taxonomy rather than clinical 'misdiagnosis', and we justify the pre-reasoning boundary operationally (end-of-problem position, before any solution token) with token-position sweeps confirming the chosen state precedes latent solution steps.
